questionStem: Three months after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery of a newborn at term, a 24-year-old woman , gravida 2, para 2, comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of pain with sexual intercourse . She breast-feeds her infant, who recently was treated for thrush. She awakens to feed him every 3 hours during the night. Her menses have not resumed . Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities . Pelvic examination shows an erythematous vagina with no discharge . The cervix is closed , and the uterus is normal in size. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.A: Recommendation for use of a lubricant

correctExplanation: Breast-feeding women are at an increased risk for atrophic vaginitis because of the antagonistic effects of prolactin on estrogen production. In women who are not breast-feeding, atrophic vaginitis commonly occurs as a postmenopausal change. Hypoestrogenemia leads to atrophic vulvovaginal changes and can present with symptoms of irritation, itching, dryness, and dyspareunia. Examination shows atrophy of the labia, decreased secretions, and mucosal erythema and friability. Treatment includes topical estrogen and the use of lubricants during sexual intercourse. Women who also require contraception can also be treated with an estrogen-containing oral contraceptive.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Pap smear testing (Choice B) employs a cervical swab to collect cells from the transformation zone and is an important screening tool for the detection of cervical carcinoma. Cervical carcinoma presents indolently until advanced, locally invasive, or metastatic; vaginal bleeding or post-coital spotting may be the presenting symptom. Dyspareunia is not a common symptom of cervical carcinoma. Vaginal culture (Choice C) is useful for the diagnosis and identification of antibiotic susceptibility of Neisseria gonorrhoeae, a Gram-negative diplococcus that can cause cervicitis, pelvic inflammatory disease, Fitz­ Hugh-Curtis syndrome, disseminated gonorrhea, septic arthritis, or urethritis. When causing vaginitis, N. gonorrhoeae typically presents with mucopurulent discharge and pruritus, although patients may be asymptomatic. Antibiotic therapy (Choice D) is useful for the treatment of sexually transmitted infections, such as Neisseria gonorrhoeae or Chlamydia trachomatis. These infections commonly cause cervicitis and present with abnormal discharge. Antifungal therapy (Choice E) is useful for treating vulvovaginitis secondary to Candida albicans. Candida! vulvovaginitis presents with signs and symptoms of vaginal pruritus, vu Ivar erythema, and thick, white discharge. This diagnosis is less likely given the patient's history of breastfeeding and absence of risk factors for candidal vulvovaginitis, such as the use of antibiotics, oral contraceptives, intravaginal or intrauterine contraceptive devices, or history of immunocompromise. Educational Objective: Breast-feeding women are at an increased risk for atrophic vaginitis because of the antagonistic effects of prolactin on estrogen production. Treatment includes topical estrogen and the use of lubricants during sexual intercourse. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 21-year-old primigravid woman at 41 weeks' gestation is admitted to the hospital in labor. Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated . Contractions occur every 3 minutes. The cervix is 100% effaced and 4 cm dilated; the vertex is at +1 station . The membranes rupture yielding moderately thick meconium-stained fluid. The fetal heart rate has a baseline of 130/min with variable decelerations lasting 45 seconds and decreasing to 60/min . Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
correctExplanation: Variable decelerations following the rupture of membranes are suggestive of umbilical cord compression. Amnioinfusion is the process of instilling fluid into the amniotic cavity. Amnioinfusion is useful for alleviating umbilical cord compression by increasing the volume of fluid in the amniotic cavity. Although amnioinfusion is the most correct response of the options provided here, evidence for the benefit of amnioinfusion towards improving outcomes related to meconium-stained amniotic fluid remains controversial.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. External cephalic version (Choice A) is a technique for repositioning the fetus when breech presentation is detected and may be performed after 37 weeks' gestation. External cephalic version is not routinely used for the management of umbilical cord compression and carries a risk of worsening compression or entanglement of the umbilical cord. Forceps delivery (Choice B) is useful for assisting vaginal delivery. If fetal distress is detected because of persistent umbilical cord compression, emergency cesarean delivery is the preferred method of delivery, rather than forceps delivery. Amniocentesis (Choice D) involves the ultrasonography-guided needle aspiration of fluid from the amniotic cavity. It is useful for the diagnosis of fetal chromosomal abnormalities and of chorioamnionitis. Removal of further amniotic fluid in the setting of cord compression is likely to worsen compression and fetal hypoxia and should not be performed. Cordocentesis (Choice E) involves the ultrasonography-guided needle aspiration of blood from the fetal umbilical cord. Sampling of fetal blood from the umbilical cord carries risk and should only be used when less invasive techniques provide inadequate or inconclusive information. It is not appropriate in the diagnosis or management of umbilical cord compression. Educational Objective: Variable decelerations following the rupture of membranes is suggestive of umbilical cord compression. Amnioinfusion is the process of instilling fluid into the amniotic cavity. Amnioinfusion is useful for alleviating fetal cord compression by increasing the volume of fluid in the amniotic cavity. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 22-year-old primigravid woman at 39 weeks' gestation has had ruptured membranes for 5 hours without contractions . Her prenatal course was uncomplicated . Her cervix is 80% effaced and 2 cm dilated. The fetal position is right occipitoposterior . The fetal heart rate pattern is shown. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this pattern?
correctExplanation: Minimal variability, which is defined as less than six beats per minute variation from the baseline heart rate, as seen in this case, can be caused by the fetal sleep state, hypoxia, opioids, and magnesium. When caused by hypoxia, the fetal heart tracing will also typically show either tachycardia or bradycardia (depending on the severity of hypoxia) along with late or variable decelerations. This can indicate uteroplacental insufficiency or umbilical cord compression, respectively. As this patient shows no sign of distress, the fetal heart rate is normal, and there has been no administration of opioids or magnesium, the minimal variability seen in this tracing is most likely caused by a fetal sleep state.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Chorioamnionitis (Choice A) is a bacterial infection of the fetal membranes and commonly occurs in premature or prolonged rupture of membranes. Maternal fever and leukocytosis are characteristic, and the uterus may be tender to palpation. A fetal heart tracing would likely show tachycardia caused by the maternal fever. --- - - - -- - - - -- - - - - -- - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - -- - - - -- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - -- - - -- -- - -- - - - - - - - - - . - - - - - - - - - - - - r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: Two days after a cesarean delivery for fetal distress , a 27-year-old woman has temperatures to 38.2°C (100 .8°F) . She had an 8-hour labor complicated by mild meconium-stained amniotic fluid . Membranes ruptured 2 hours after admission . Breath sounds are decreased at both lung bases . Abdominal examination shows mild tenderness below the umbilicus and a well-healing incision . There is a moderate amount of lochia with no odor. Examination of the lower extremities shows edema and no tenderness . Her hemoglobin concentration is 10.8 g/dl , leukocyte count is 14,000/mm 3, and platelet count is 189,000/mm 3. A urine catheter specimen is negative . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? A Atelectasis G) Pulmonary embolism
correctExplanation: Atelectasis refers to the partial or complete collapse or incomplete expansion of pulmonary parenchyma. There are multiple types of atelectasis, including obstructive, passive, compressive, cicatricial, and adhesive. It is most common in patients who are gravid, immobile, or in the postsurgical state, who are unable to produce adequate tidal volume to expand the lungs. In gravid patients or patients who have just undergone vaginal delivery, increased intra-abdominal pressure, caused by the gravid uterus, pushes on the diaphragm and intrathoracic cavity thus decreasing the ability of the lungs to expand normally. Physical examination will show diminished respiratory effort, often with reduced breath sounds at the lung bases corresponding to the regions of non-aerated, collapsed lung and inadequate diaphragmatic excursion. Pain control, incentive spirometry, and respiratory therapy with lung expansion maneuvers are key initial steps in management.
incorrectExplanation: nd K. Deep venous thrombosis (Choice B) formation is promoted with venous stasis, endothelial injury, and hypercoagulability. It would typically present with unilateral extremity edema. Endometritis (Choice C) is an acute, typically polymicrobial, infection of the uterine endometrium. Patients typically present with fever, tenderness of the uterine fundus, and mucopurulent vaginal discharge. A risk factor for the development of endometritis includes prolonged rupture of membranes (greater than 18 hours) and would be unlikely in this patient. Episiotomy infection (Choice D) would present with induration, erythema, and purulent drainage from an episiotomy incision placed during delivery. It would be unlikely in this patient with a well-healing incision. Mastitis (Choice E) presents with erythema and induration in an area of tender, warm skin of the breast. It classically occurs in breastfeeding mothers as a consequence of nipple trauma leading to inoculation from cutaneous or oral flora. It would be unlikely in this patient just after delivery. Pneumonia (Choice F) is characterized by fever, a cough productive of sputum, malaise, and chest discomfort. On physical examination, there may be abnormal lung sounds such as rales or rhonchi, along with increased tactile fremitus. Pulmonary embolism (Choice G) is characteristically associated with long periods of immobilization and deep venous thrombosis formation from venous stasis. Classic symptoms include pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea; if a pulmonary infarction occurs, hemoptysis may be present. Vital signs are often notable for tachycardia, tachypnea, and hypoxia. Pyelonephritis (Choice H) and urinary tract infection (Choice K) would present with pyuria, leukocyte esterase, and nitrites. Lower urinary tract infections would present with dysuria, urinary urgency, and frequency, and pyelonephritis may present with flank pain, nausea, and vomiting. Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis (Choice I) is a rare sequela of endometritis that can lead to local invasion and infection of the pelvic vein walls, which causes intimal damage and thrombosis. This condition typically presents with pelvic pain and fever, which is often widely variable in course, ranging from normal temperature to extremely high. Diagnosis typically occurs through blood cultures. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous
